## Executive Summary & Product Vision

---

### 1.1 The Problem We Are Solving

Large enterprises running SAFe (Scaled Agile Framework) face a structural paradox: the framework that promises alignment and predictability consistently breaks down at the exact moments it matters most. Program Increment (PI) Planning events — the heartbeat ritual of any Agile Release Train — consume 2–4 days, 50–300 people, and R$80,000–R$150,000 in direct costs per cycle for a 1–2 ART organisation. Despite this investment, teams routinely emerge from PI Planning with dependency maps drawn on whiteboards that become stale within 72 hours, risk registers that live in spreadsheets no one updates, and PI Objectives whose business value scores are negotiated in hallway conversations rather than derived from strategic data.

The problem is not the framework. The problem is that no tool purpose-built for SAFe orchestration exists at a price point and data-sovereignty posture that mid-market Brazilian and Latin American enterprises can accept. Jira Align starts at $30–$40 per user per month with a minimum seat commitment that prices out any organisation with fewer than 500 seats. Planview targets Fortune 500 portfolio offices with six-figure implementation contracts. Both products require cloud data residency, which creates a hard blocker for financial services, healthcare, government contractors, and any enterprise operating under LGPD or sector-specific data localisation mandates.

Cosmos/Nebuloz is built on a single, falsifiable market hypothesis:

> **Large enterprises need SAFe orchestration with AI assistance that runs entirely inside their own infrastructure, and PI Planning is the highest-pain entry point because it is simultaneously the most expensive ritual, the most chaotic coordination problem, and the most measurable outcome in the entire SAFe cadence.**

---

### 1.2 Product Vision Statement

**Cosmos/Nebuloz** is a SAFe 6.0 enterprise Agile management platform that transforms how Agile Release Trains plan, execute, and learn. It delivers a complete SAFe toolchain — from Portfolio Kanban and Lean Budget governance through PI Planning orchestration, Program Board visualisation, Sprint execution, and continuous flow metrics — augmented by a native AI copilot (LACE) that runs on the customer's own infrastructure, processes no data externally, and speaks the precise vocabulary of SAFe 6.0.

**Vision:** Every ART in Latin America operates with the planning precision, dependency visibility, and continuous-improvement discipline that Fortune 100 companies achieve with ten-times-larger tooling budgets.

**Mission:** Eliminate the coordination tax in scaled Agile programmes by making SAFe orchestration radically accessible, AI-augmented, and data-sovereign.

---

### 1.3 Target Personas

#### Persona P-01 — Release Train Engineer (RTE)

**Profile:** The RTE owns the PI Planning ceremony end-to-end. They facilitate breakout sessions, track cross-team dependencies, surface ROAM risks, aggregate confidence votes, and are ultimately accountable for whether the ART delivers committed PI Objectives. In Brazilian enterprises, the RTE role is frequently held by a senior Scrum Master or an Agile Coach promoted into the position, often without dedicated tooling beyond Miro boards and spreadsheets.

**Primary pain points:**
- No single view of all inter-team dependencies across the ART during live planning sessions
- Confidence vote aggregation done manually via show-of-hands or ad-hoc polling tools disconnected from the PI Plan
- Risk ROAM status tracked in a separate spreadsheet, never linked to the features or teams that own remediation
- No historical data to benchmark PI Objective predictability across cycles

**Jobs to be done:**
- Facilitate live PI Planning sessions with real-time visibility into team breakout progress
- Generate and distribute the Program Board before the session closes
- Aggregate and publish the PI Objectives package to business stakeholders
- Track ROAM risks through the PI execution window

**Value proposition of Cosmos:** A single facilitation console with live session state (powered by Liveblocks), integrated confidence voting, auto-generated Program Board, and a LACE AI assistant that surfaces risk patterns and dependency bottlenecks on demand.

---

#### Persona P-02 — Product Owner / Team Product Owner (PO/TPO)

**Profile:** Owns the team backlog and is responsible for decomposing Features into Stories, setting acceptance criteria, and committing team capacity to PI Objectives. In larger ARTs (8+ teams), the PO often receives Features that were negotiated at the Epic level without clear implementation guidance. They frequently operate under incomplete context about upstream dependencies and strategic theme alignment.

**Primary pain points:**
- Features arrive from Portfolio with vague hypothesis statements and no leading indicators
- Story decomposition is manual and unconstrained — no AI-assisted breakdown available
- WSJF scoring is subjective and inconsistent across teams within the same ART
- Cannot visualise how their team's committed stories affect downstream teams' capacity

**Jobs to be done:**
- Break Features into implementation-ready Stories during PI Planning breakout sessions
- Score Features using WSJF with enough data to make scoring defensible in PI Planning reviews
- Communicate team capacity constraints to the RTE before the Draft Plan Review
- Track PI Objective achievement through the execution window

**Value proposition of Cosmos:** AI-assisted Feature decomposition via LACE, WSJF scoring with weighted inputs and ART-level consistency scoring, real-time capacity visualisation, and PI Objective tracking dashboards.

---

#### Persona P-03 — System Architect / Solution Architect (SA)

**Profile:** Accountable for architectural runway, NFR governance, and identifying Enabler work that must be sequenced before Feature delivery. In practice, the SA is often pulled into PI Planning as a point-of-escalation for technical feasibility questions and spends the session in reactive firefighting rather than proactive runway planning.

**Primary pain points:**
- No structured way to surface NFR violations against Features being committed during PI Planning
- Enabler Features compete with Business Features for team capacity with no algorithmic prioritisation support
- Architectural decisions made in breakout sessions are not captured in a persistent knowledge base
- Cannot see which Stories across all teams carry the highest technical risk

**Jobs to be done:**
- Review and approve Feature NFRs before PI Planning commits
- Ensure architectural runway is adequately funded in the Lean Budget allocation
- Flag technical risks to the RTE during the PI session
- Maintain a living architectural knowledge base accessible to all teams

**Value proposition of Cosmos:** NFR governance linked to the Epic model, Enabler Feature tagging and prioritisation, LACE knowledge extraction from PI Planning sessions, and an architectural decisions log surfaced through the copilot.

---

#### Persona P-04 — Business Owner (BO)

**Profile:** An executive stakeholder — VP of Product, CTO, Head of Digital — who sponsors the ART financially and provides the business context for PI Objectives. Business Owners assign business value scores (1–10) to PI Objectives and are the final arbiters of scope trade-offs during the Draft Plan Review. They attend PI Planning for two half-days and then disappear into their calendars, receiving no further structured updates until the PI System Demo.

**Primary pain points:**
- PI Objective business value scoring happens in the room with no data support
- No way to track planned vs. achieved business value across PIs without manually requesting reports
- Portfolio-level investment visibility requires manual aggregation from team-level tools
- Cannot connect strategic OKRs to ground-level Sprint delivery without an analyst in the loop

**Jobs to be done:**
- Assign business value to PI Objectives during planning with contextual data support
- Receive automated PI Objective achievement reports at PI close
- Track portfolio-level investment allocation vs. strategic theme coverage
- Review roadmap confidence trends over time

**Value proposition of Cosmos:** Business Owner dashboard with PI Objective tracking, automated PI close reports, Lean Budget visualisation tied to strategic themes, and OKR-to-Story traceability.

---

#### Persona P-05 — Scrum Master (SM)

**Profile:** Facilitates Sprint ceremonies, removes impediments, coaches the team on SAFe practices, and feeds team-level metrics upward to the RTE. In practice, the SM is the heaviest daily user of any Agile management tool — they live in the Sprint board, standup interface, impediment log, and retrospective tools.

**Primary pain points:**
- Sprint board, impediment tracker, standup log, and retrospective tool are in three different systems
- Velocity and capacity data must be manually exported to be shared with the RTE
- Impediment escalation to ART level has no structured workflow
- Retrospective action items are captured but rarely tracked to completion

**Jobs to be done:**
- Run daily standup with blockers surfaced and linked to impediments
- Track Sprint velocity and capacity against PI Plan commitments
- Escalate impediments to ART level when they exceed team resolution authority
- Facilitate retrospectives and track action items to closure

**Value proposition of Cosmos:** Unified Sprint execution console (board, standup, retrospective, impediment log), automated velocity capture, structured impediment escalation to RTE dashboard, and retrospective action item tracking with LACE improvement suggestions.

---

#### Persona P-06 — Development Team Member (Dev/QA)

**Profile:** Executes Stories and Tasks, logs blockers in standups, participates in retrospectives, and provides estimates during PI Planning. They interact with the tool daily but have the lowest tolerance for friction — any workflow requiring more than three clicks to update a Story status will be abandoned.

**Primary pain points:**
- Standup entry is a form-filling exercise with no intelligence — blocked items are not automatically elevated
- Task estimation has no historical calibration to team velocity
- Defect tracking is disconnected from the Story that generated the defect
- No visibility into how their work connects to PI Objectives or strategic themes

**Jobs to be done:**
- Update Story and Task status with minimal friction
- Log standups including blockers in under 60 seconds
- File defects linked to the originating Story
- See how their Sprint work contributes to ART-level PI Objectives

**Value proposition of Cosmos:** Keyboard-driven Sprint board, standup with automatic blocker detection and SM notification, Defect-to-Story linking, and a personal contribution view tracing Tasks → Stories → Features → PI Objectives → Strategic Themes.

### 1.4 The Wedge Strategy

#### 1.4.1 Primary Wedge — PI Planning Orchestration

PI Planning is the highest-density coordination event in the SAFe calendar. For a 1–2 ART organisation (50–200 participants), a single PI Planning cycle represents:

- **R$80,000–R$150,000** in direct salary cost (2–4 days × headcount × average loaded daily rate)
- **2–4 hours** of setup time per team for capacity loading before the session
- **4–8 hours** of manual post-session work to publish the Program Board, PI Objectives package, and Risk ROAM register
- **100% of ART commitment** set for the next 8–12 weeks in a 2–4 day window — the highest-leverage planning event in the organisation

The PI Planning module is the land-and-expand entry point. A prospect who adopts Cosmos for PI Planning facilitation alone generates immediate, measurable ROI (time saved in session setup, facilitation, and post-session documentation). Once the PI Plan exists in Cosmos, the natural expansion path is: Sprint execution (teams) → Risks and Dependencies (RTE) → Portfolio Kanban (executive) → LACE AI (all personas).

**Wedge hypothesis for customer discovery interviews:**
> "If we could reduce your PI Planning post-session documentation work from 4–8 hours to under 30 minutes, and give your RTE a live dependency map during breakout sessions rather than post-hoc, would that justify a tool change even if we didn't have full Portfolio management yet?"

---

#### 1.4.2 Secondary Wedge — LACE AI Copilot (Data-Sovereign)

The AI copilot (LACE — Learn, Adapt, Coach, Enable) is the secondary wedge for organisations that have already tried GitHub Copilot for code but have no AI augmentation for their Agile management processes. LACE is positioned explicitly as an **infra-local AI** — the model and all embeddings run on the customer's own infrastructure (on-premise or private VPC), no PI Planning data, Strategic Themes, or PI Objectives leave the customer's environment.

This data-sovereignty posture is a hard requirement for:
- Brazilian financial services firms operating under BACEN Resolution 4,893/2021
- Healthcare organisations under CFM/LGPD data localisation requirements
- Government contractors and public sector agencies
- Any enterprise that has blocked SaaS AI tools at the CISO level due to data leakage concerns

**Secondary wedge hypothesis for customer discovery interviews:**
> "If your CISO has blocked ChatGPT and Copilot for planning-related work because of data classification concerns, would an AI copilot that runs entirely on your own infrastructure — same capabilities, zero external API calls — change that decision?"

### 1.5 Module Surface Overview

Cosmos/Nebuloz exposes a comprehensive SAFe 6.0 toolchain across the following functional domains:

**Portfolio Layer:**
- `portfolio` — Portfolio Kanban with Epic lifecycle management (FUNNEL → IMPLEMENTING → DONE)
- `epics` — Epic canvas with Lean Business Case, hypothesis statements, leading indicators, and WSJF scoring
- `solution-trains` — Solution Train coordination above the ART level
- `strategic-themes` — Strategic Theme definition with horizon planning and ART alignment
- `lean-budget` — Lean Budget guardrails with CapEx/OpEx allocation per ART per PI
- `roadmap` — Rolling roadmap with confidence intervals and Epic-to-quarter mapping
- `okrs` — Objectives and Key Results linked to teams, ARTs, and Strategic Themes

**Program Layer (ART):**
- `arts` — ART configuration, team roster, velocity baselines, and governance settings
- `pi-planning` — Full PI Planning orchestration: session management, confidence voting, Program Board, PI Objectives
- `dependencies` — Cross-team and cross-ART dependency map with DependencyLink lifecycle
- `risks` — Risk register with ROAM status workflow and ART-level escalation
- `features` — Feature backlog with WSJF scoring, NFR governance, and Story decomposition
- `program-board` — Visual Program Board with iteration columns and dependency arcs
- `analytics` — ART-level flow metrics: throughput, cycle time, predictability index, PI Objective completion rate

**Team Layer:**
- `teams` — Team configuration, capacity planning, member management, and velocity history
- `sprints` — Sprint lifecycle management with board, burndown, and velocity capture
- `stories` — Story management with acceptance criteria, task decomposition, and defect linking
- `workflows` — BPMN-modelled team workflows with XState execution
- `standup` — Daily standup with blocker detection and SM notification
- `retrospective` — Sprint retrospective with structured Well/Improve/Action format and action item tracking

**AI & Intelligence Layer:**
- `copilot` — LACE AI copilot interface with streaming responses via Vercel AI SDK
- `lace` — LACE knowledge management: vector store, embedding pipeline, retrieval-augmented generation
- `flow-intelligence` — AI-generated flow bottleneck detection and improvement recommendations
- `safe-copilot` — SAFe-specific prompt library and guardrails for LACE responses

**Platform Layer:**
- `integrations` — Webhook and API integration framework
- `notifications` — Event-driven notification engine (in-app, email, Slack)
- `settings` — Organisation, ART, and user-level configuration
- `permissions` — Role-based access control with SAFe-aligned role taxonomy
- `audit` — Immutable audit log for compliance and SOC2 Type II readiness
- `billing` — Subscription management and seat-based pricing engine
- `search` — Cross-entity full-text and semantic search
- `onboarding` — Guided onboarding for new RTEs, POs, and SMs

### 1.6 Competitive Thesis

#### 1.6.1 Jira Align

**What it does well:** Deep Jira integration, established brand trust in enterprises already running Atlassian stacks, comprehensive SAFe terminology coverage, large partner ecosystem.

**Where it fails large enterprises considering Cosmos:**

| Dimension | Jira Align | Cosmos/Nebuloz |
|---|---|---|
| Pricing floor | ~$30–$40/user/month, 100-seat minimum | Seat-based, no minimum, SMB-accessible tiers |
| Data sovereignty | Cloud-only (Atlassian cloud) | Infra-local deployment option |
| AI copilot | Generic Atlassian Intelligence (not SAFe-specific) | LACE: SAFe-specific, runs on customer infra |
| PI Planning facilitation | Sync via Jira boards, not purpose-built for live session | Native PISession model with real-time collab |
| Onboarding complexity | 3–6 month implementation engagement typical | Self-serve onboarding wizard in < 2 hours |
| Latin America support | English-first, no PT-BR SAFe terminology | PT-BR native, BR-localised role vocabulary |

**Jira Align customer discovery question:**
> "What percentage of your teams actually use Jira Align vs. keeping their real work in individual Jira projects? If the answer is less than 80%, what is preventing adoption?"

---

#### 1.6.2 Planview

**What it does well:** Enterprise portfolio management at Fortune 500 scale, deep financial planning integration, Lean-Agile hybrid support, established relationships with PMO offices.

**Where it fails large enterprises considering Cosmos:**

| Dimension | Planview | Cosmos/Nebuloz |
|---|---|---|
| Target segment | Fortune 500, $5M+ ACV deals | R$50K–R$500K ARR, 1–10 ART orgs |
| Implementation time | 6–18 months with SI partner | < 30 days self-serve |
| SAFe specificity | Framework-agnostic (supports SAFe, PRINCE2, etc.) | SAFe 6.0 native — no configuration needed |
| AI augmentation | Roadmap-level AI, no Sprint/PI execution AI | LACE operates at all SAFe levels |
| Real-time collaboration | Not a core capability | Liveblocks-powered live PI Planning sessions |

**Planview customer discovery question:**
> "At what point in your growth trajectory did you feel Planview became the right tool? What were you using before, and what made you willing to invest in an SI engagement?"

---

#### 1.6.3 Rally (Broadcom)

Rally (formerly CA Agile Central) represents the legacy incumbent in this space — feature-complete, deeply entrenched in large enterprises, but technologically stagnant post-Broadcom acquisition.

**Where Cosmos wins against Rally:**
- Modern UI/UX (Next.js 16, React 19) vs. Rally's dated interface
- AI-native architecture vs. no AI roadmap publicly announced
- Active development velocity (weekly releases) vs. Broadcom's maintenance-mode cadence
- Pricing transparency vs. Broadcom's opaque enterprise negotiation model

### 1.7 Core Market Hypothesis Validation Plan

#### MH-01 — The PI Planning Pain Hypothesis

**Hypothesis:** RTEs at 1–2 ART organisations in Brazil spend 4–8 hours post-PI-Planning on manual documentation that Cosmos can reduce to under 30 minutes.

**Validation method:** Time-and-motion study in 5 prospect PI Planning sessions (observer role, no tool intervention). Measure: time from session close to published PI Objectives package, Program Board, and Risk ROAM register.

**Success threshold:** ≥4 of 5 observed sessions exceed 4 hours of post-session documentation work.

**Interview questions:**
1. "Walk me through what happens in the 48 hours after your PI Planning event closes. Who does what, in which tools?"
2. "What is the first thing that goes wrong with your PI Plan in the first two weeks of execution?"
3. "If you had to quantify the cost of PI Planning including prep, facilitation, and post-session cleanup, what number would you put on it?"

---

#### MH-02 — The Data Sovereignty Blocker Hypothesis

**Hypothesis:** ≥40% of Brazilian enterprises in financial services, healthcare, and government contracting have a CISO-level block on SaaS AI tools for planning data, and an infra-local AI deployment model would remove that block.

**Validation method:** Security posture interviews with CISOs and IT compliance officers at 10 target accounts. Direct question: "Is there a current policy blocking AI tools that process planning or strategy data on external infrastructure?"

**Success threshold:** ≥4 of 10 accounts confirm an active policy block that an infra-local deployment would resolve.

**Interview questions:**
1. "What is your current classification level for PI Planning data — internal, confidential, or restricted?"
2. "Has your CISO's office issued any guidance on AI tools that process strategic planning content?"
3. "If we could provide an AI copilot that runs entirely in your private VPC with zero external API calls, would that change your ability to adopt it?"

---

#### MH-03 — The Jira Alignment Gap Hypothesis

**Hypothesis:** Enterprises running Jira Align have < 70% active adoption across their ART teams, with teams reverting to flat Jira projects for actual Sprint execution.

**Validation method:** Product usage interviews with RTEs and SMs at 8 Jira Align customers. Proxy metric: "What percentage of your stories are created inside Jira Align versus directly in team-level Jira projects?"

**Success threshold:** ≥5 of 8 accounts report < 70% story creation through the Jira Align hierarchy.

---

#### MH-04 — The Latin America SAFe Localisation Hypothesis

**Hypothesis:** Brazilian SAFe practitioners report that English-language tooling creates a meaningful friction cost in training and adoption, and PT-BR-native tooling would accelerate internal change management.

**Validation method:** Survey of 50 Brazilian RTEs and SMs sourced from the Brazilian SAFe community (SAFe Brasil network, LinkedIn groups). Question: "How much of your Agile tooling is available in Portuguese, and does language affect adoption speed in your organisation?"

**Success threshold:** ≥60% report that full PT-BR localisation would meaningfully reduce adoption friction.

---

### 1.8 Investment Thesis Summary

For investor due diligence, the Cosmos/Nebuloz thesis rests on four compounding advantages:

**1. Regulatory moat.** LGPD, BACEN, and sector-specific data localisation requirements create a structural barrier against cloud-only competitors in the largest enterprise segments in Brazil. Cosmos's infra-local deployment model is not a feature — it is a compliance requirement that competitors cannot satisfy without fundamental architecture changes.

**2. SAFe specificity as a defensible niche.** General-purpose project management tools (Jira, Monday, Asana, Linear) cannot credibly claim SAFe expertise without dedicated product investment. By building native SAFe 6.0 data models (PIPlan, PIObjective, ROAM, WSJF, Lean Budget), Cosmos speaks the practitioner's language in a way that horizontal tools cannot replicate without multi-year development commitment.

**3. AI-first architecture at the right layer.** The copilot integration is not a GPT wrapper on top of a legacy data model. LACE operates on a purpose-built knowledge graph (PIKnowledgeVector, semantic search, flow intelligence) that makes its outputs contextually accurate for SAFe processes. Competitors retrofitting AI onto existing data models will produce generic outputs; LACE produces SAFe-specific, ART-specific, PI-specific guidance.

**4. Land-and-expand with a natural seat expansion curve.** The PI Planning wedge acquires the RTE and a small admin seat. Once the PI Plan exists in Cosmos, every team member (SM, PO, Dev) becomes a natural seat addition. A 2-ART organisation with 10 teams of 8 people represents 160 seats from a single PI Planning sale. The expansion motion is structurally embedded in the product architecture.

**Total Addressable Market (TAM) framing:**
- Brazil has approximately 2,400 enterprises with 500+ employees actively running SAFe or SAFe-adjacent scaled Agile (source: State of Agile Report 2024, adjusted for Brazil market penetration)
- Average ART size: 80–120 people
- Target ASP: R$120–R$300/seat/year at 60–80 seats per ART
- Serviceable Addressable Market (SAM): R$350M–R$900M/year in Brazil alone
- Serviceable Obtainable Market (SOM) at 3% penetration in 36 months: R$10M–R$27M ARR

### 1.9 Product Naming and Brand Context

**Cosmos** is the internal product name used in engineering, documentation, and investor materials. It references the orbital metaphor that runs through the product's visual design language — ARTs as orbital rings, Features as satellites, Strategic Themes as gravitational centres.

**Nebuloz** is the market-facing brand name for the Brazilian market. The name references the nebula — the formative cloud from which ordered structures emerge — as a metaphor for transforming the chaos of scaled Agile coordination into a coherent, navigable system.

Both names are used interchangeably in this document. In customer-facing materials, Nebuloz is preferred. In technical documentation and API references, Cosmos is used.
