- **AC-15.10.2** — Given the vote collection phase, when a participant views another user's vote widget, then the specific vote value is not visible (only "voted / not voted" status is shown).
- **AC-15.10.3** — Given aggregate score < 3.0, when reveal occurs, then the RTE's UI displays a prompt to re-open discussion before committing the plan.
- **AC-15.10.4** — Given a participant attempts to vote after reveal, then the vote widget is disabled and the attempt is silently ignored.

#### Business Rules

- Vote values are restricted to integers 1–5.
- Vote values for a user are stored under a per-user Liveblocks storage key; other users' read permissions on vote values are blocked until `voteSessionStatus === REVEALED`.
- Maximum one open `ConfidenceVoteSession` per `PISession` at any time.
- Reveal is irreversible; `voteSessionStatus` cannot revert from REVEALED to OPEN.
- A second round may be started by the RTE only after the current round is REVEALED and persisted.
- Vote session data is retained in PostgreSQL indefinitely for audit purposes.

#### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** The "simultaneous reveal" mechanic in Fist-of-Five prevents social anchoring — if votes are revealed sequentially, participants bias toward earlier votes. Remote teams using polls with visible running totals report vote anchoring as a problem. The private-then-simultaneous reveal directly preserves the integrity of the SAFe ceremony.

**Target segment:** RTEs running remote PI Planning who have experienced anchoring effects with standard polling tools (Mentimeter, Slido) and want a purpose-built SAFe-compliant experience.

**Key interview question:** "When running confidence votes remotely, have you noticed that participants tend to match the first few votes they see? How have you tried to address that?"

---

### 15.6 Collaborative Surfaces Outside PI Planning

#### Description

Liveblocks is not exclusive to PI Planning. Presence and concurrent editing are active across additional surfaces where real-time awareness meaningfully reduces coordination overhead. Each surface uses the same room topology (`{orgId}:{surface}:{entityId}`) and the same auth handshake.

#### 15.6.1 Portfolio Kanban

- Epic cards on the Portfolio Kanban (`org:portfolio-kanban:{orgId}`) broadcast presence and support concurrent status updates via Yjs.
- When a PM drags an Epic from `ANALYZING` to `PORTFOLIO_BACKLOG`, all other portfolio stakeholders see the move instantly.
- Concurrent drag conflicts resolve via Yjs last-write-wins; a toast notifies the losing user.
- Room is always open (not session-gated); any MEMBER or above may connect.

#### 15.6.2 Sprint Board

- Each Sprint has a dedicated room: `org:sprint-board:{sprintId}`.
- Story cards support concurrent status moves (To Do → In Progress → Done) and point estimation.
- Presence shows which SM or developer is actively touching which card during daily standup or sprint planning.
- Room is created when the Sprint is created and archived 30 days after `Sprint.status = CLOSED`.

#### 15.6.3 BPMN Workflow Canvas

- Each `bpmnDefinition` in a Team has a room: `org:bpmn:{bpmnDefinitionId}`.
- BPMN-JS 18 elements (tasks, gateways, flows) are stored as Liveblocks Yjs XML fragments.
- Concurrent edits to different BPMN elements are merged by Yjs; concurrent edits to the same element are last-write-wins.
- SA and SM can collaborate on process definitions during PI Planning breakout sessions.

#### 15.6.4 Retrospective Board

- Each Retrospective has a room: `org:retrospective:{retrospectiveId}`.
- `wellItems`, `improveItems`, and `actionItems` are Yjs arrays.
- Team members concurrently add, edit, and vote on items.
- Voting is public (no private-then-reveal mechanic); vote counts update in real time.
- Room closes 7 days after `Retrospective` is created.

#### Acceptance Criteria (cross-surface)

- **AC-15.06.1** — Given any collaborative surface room, when a user with VIEWER role connects, then all edit controls are disabled and the user is in observe-only mode.
- **AC-15.06.2** — Given a Sprint Board room, when 30 days have elapsed after the sprint closes, then the room is archived and new connections return a 410 Gone response with a message directing to the read-only historical view.
- **AC-15.06.3** — Given a BPMN canvas with 2 users editing different elements, when both save, then both changes are preserved without either overwriting the other.

#### Business Rules

- Maximum active rooms per tenant: determined by plan tier (FREE = 5 concurrent, STARTER = 25, PROFESSIONAL = 100, ENTERPRISE = unlimited).
- Room archival is triggered by an Inngest scheduled job, not by the last client disconnect.
- All rooms enforce the same tenant-scoped auth handshake; no cross-tenant room sharing is possible by design.

#### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** Teams use Miro or FigJam for retrospectives and BPMN whiteboards alongside their backlog tool, creating a fragmented toolchain. Embedding collaboration natively in the same surface where work is tracked eliminates the context switch and keeps artifacts co-located with the entities they describe.

**Target segment:** Scrum Masters and SAs at organizations already paying for ≥2 separate collaboration tools (Miro + Jira, Confluence + Miro) who cite tool sprawl as a pain point.

**Key interview question:** "How many separate tools does your team use during a single PI Planning event, and where do artifacts from those tools end up after the event closes?"

---

### 15.7 Conflict Resolution and Storage Consistency Model

#### Description

Cosmos uses a dual-write consistency model: Liveblocks Yjs CRDT is the live view; PostgreSQL is the durable record. This section defines how conflicts are resolved, how the two stores stay in sync, and what guarantees are made to users.

#### Conflict Resolution Rules

| Field Type | Resolution Strategy | User Notification |
|---|---|---|
| Card position / iterationId | Last-write-wins (Yjs) | Toast to losing user |
| Rich text (TipTap descriptions) | Yjs OT character merge | None — seamless |
| Numeric fields (businessValue, points) | Last-write-wins (Yjs) | Toast to losing user |
| Status transitions (card status) | Last-write-wins (Yjs) | Toast to losing user |
| Boolean flags (stretch, blocked) | Last-write-wins (Yjs) | None |
| DependencyLink arrows | Last-write-wins (Yjs) | Toast to losing user |
| Vote values | Last-write-wins pre-reveal; immutable post-reveal | Toast pre-reveal |

#### Storage Sync Flow

1. **Hydration (room join):** On the first client connecting to an empty room, the server action reads from PostgreSQL and writes the canonical state into Liveblocks storage. Subsequent clients receive Liveblocks state directly.
2. **Live mutations:** Client writes to Liveblocks Yjs; a debounced server action (300 ms default, 0 ms for status transitions) persists to PostgreSQL.
3. **Flush on session close:** When PISession transitions to CLOSED, a server action performs a full flush — reads the final Liveblocks storage state and overwrites PostgreSQL. This guarantees the durable record matches the collaborative session.
4. **Conflict detection:** PostgreSQL writes use optimistic concurrency (Prisma `version` field on mutable entities). If a flush encounters a version mismatch, the server logs a `STORAGE_CONFLICT` audit event and the Liveblocks state wins (last-write-wins at the persistent layer on explicit session close).

#### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-15.07.1** — Given a room hydration event, when the first client connects to an empty room, then the Liveblocks storage matches the PostgreSQL state within 1 s.
- **AC-15.07.2** — Given PISession transitions to CLOSED, then a full flush from Liveblocks to PostgreSQL completes within 5 s, verified by the session's `status` and an AuditLog entry `PI_SESSION_FLUSHED`.
- **AC-15.07.3** — Given a PostgreSQL version conflict during a debounced write, then the conflict is logged as `STORAGE_CONFLICT` in AuditLog and the Liveblocks value is treated as authoritative without crashing the session.

#### Business Rules

- Liveblocks storage for a PISession is retained for 90 days after the session closes; after that, the room is purged (Liveblocks API `deleteRoom`).
- PostgreSQL remains the system of record for reporting, analytics, and integrations; Liveblocks is never queried by integration sync jobs.
- The flush-on-close operation is idempotent; retrying it produces the same PostgreSQL state.
- If Liveblocks is unreachable for > 60 s, the UI shows a "Collaboration unavailable — working in local mode" banner; local mutations are queued in Zustand and replayed on reconnect.

#### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** Teams that use optimistic UI with eventual consistency report confusion when changes "disappear" or revert unexpectedly. By making Liveblocks the live authority and PostgreSQL the durable record with explicit flush semantics, Cosmos provides predictable behavior that builds user trust — a key differentiator over tools where "save" semantics are opaque.

**Target segment:** Enterprise Agile programs with compliance requirements (SOC2, ISO 27001) that need a clear audit trail of who changed what during planning events.

**Key interview question:** "Has your team ever had a PI plan change disappear or revert after a remote planning session? What was the impact and how did you resolve it?"

---

## OKRs, Strategic Themes & Roadmap

---

### Overview

This section specifies the strategy-to-execution alignment layer of Cosmos. It covers four interconnected capabilities: OKR management with key result tracking and quarterly snapshots, strategic themes with ART linkage, the strategy map connecting themes to portfolio outcomes, and roadmap items that bind epics to delivery quarters. Together these capabilities form the platform's core value proposition for CTO and VP Strategy buyers: full traceability from enterprise intent down to sprint stories, eliminating the gap between strategy decks and delivery actuals that characterizes incumbent tools.

---

### 16.1 OKR Management

#### Description

OKR management enables RTEs, Business Owners, and Portfolio Managers to define Objectives and Key Results at both the ART level and the individual team level, track key result progress through quarterly snapshots, and surface alignment gaps where team-level OKRs drift from ART-level intent. The model mirrors the `OKR { id, artId, teamId, objective, keyResults[], quarter, year }` and `KeyResult { id, okrId, description, target, current, unit, snapshots[] }` domain structures, supporting per-key-result unit configuration (percentage, count, currency, ratio) and snapshot history for trend visualization.

The critical differentiator is bidirectional linkage: OKRs cascade down to epics via `Epic.strategicThemeId` and surface up to portfolio dashboards, creating a live, auditable chain from enterprise objective to story acceptance.

#### Actors / Personas

- **RTE (Release Train Engineer):** Owns ART-level OKRs, monitors team alignment, escalates misalignment to portfolio.
- **Business Owner:** Reviews OKR health during PI Planning and quarterly business reviews (QBR); approves strategic direction.
- **Portfolio Manager / VP Strategy:** Consumes rolled-up OKR health across ARTs; uses for board reporting.
- **Product Manager (PM):** Maps epics and features to OKRs; ensures delivery backlog reflects strategic priorities.
- **Team PM / PO:** Owns team-level OKRs; updates key result current values each sprint or on demand.
- **SAFe Copilot (AI actor):** Detects OKR staleness, drafts key result suggestions, flags confidence anomalies.

---

#### 16.1.1 Create and Edit OKR

##### Description

Allows RTEs and PMs to create an OKR for a given ART or team, specify the objective text, define one to five key results with target values and measurement units, assign the quarter and year, and link the OKR to one or more strategic themes. Inline editing is supported post-creation. Archived OKRs from prior quarters are read-only but queryable.

##### Use Cases

**UC-01: Create ART-level OKR**

- **Trigger:** RTE opens the OKR module for the current ART and clicks "New OKR".
- **Pre-condition:** User has `RTE` or `PORTFOLIO_MANAGER` role on the org. At least one ART exists.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. User selects scope: ART (pre-filled from current context) or Team.
  2. User enters objective text (max 200 chars).
  3. User sets quarter (Q1–Q4) and year.
  4. User adds 1–5 key results: description, target value, unit (%, count, $, ratio, custom string).
  5. User optionally links OKR to one or more strategic themes via multi-select dropdown.
  6. User clicks Save. System persists OKR with `current = 0` for all key results, `status = ACTIVE`.
  7. System broadcasts a `okr.created` event; Copilot queues a suggestion run to propose leading indicators.
  8. OKR appears in the ART OKR list, sorted by quarter descending.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (duplicate objective text in same quarter): System shows a warning "An OKR with similar objective exists for Q{n} {year}" with a link to the existing record. User may proceed or cancel.
  - A2 (no strategic theme linked): System persists with a `UNLINKED` tag and surfaces the OKR in the alignment gap report.
- **Exceptions:**
  - E1 (missing objective text or target): Form validation prevents save; inline field-level error messages.
  - E2 (artId not found): API returns 404; UI shows "ART not found. Reload and try again."

**UC-02: Edit OKR Objective or Key Results**

- **Trigger:** RTE clicks Edit on an existing active OKR.
- **Pre-condition:** OKR `status = ACTIVE`. Quarter has not closed (current date before quarter end + 30 days grace).
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System opens inline editor pre-filled with current values.
  2. User modifies objective text and/or key result targets/units.
  3. User saves. System records an audit log entry: actor, timestamp, field changed, old value, new value.
  4. If target value changed for a key result that already has snapshots, system flags "Target revised mid-quarter" on the key result card.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (quarter is closed): Edit is blocked; user sees "This OKR is from a closed quarter and cannot be modified."
  - A2 (key result deleted that has snapshot history): System soft-deletes; snapshots are retained and shown as "Removed Key Result" in historical views.

**UC-03: Archive OKR at Quarter Close**

- **Trigger:** Automated cron job fires on first day after quarter end, OR RTE manually triggers "Close Quarter" from the OKR settings panel.
- **Pre-condition:** OKR `status = ACTIVE`, quarter end date passed.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System sets OKR `status = ARCHIVED`.
  2. System captures a final snapshot for all key results with `current` value at time of close.
  3. System computes final achievement rate: `(current / target) * 100` per key result; stores as `finalAchievement` on the key result.
  4. RTE and Business Owner receive an in-app notification: "Q{n} OKRs closed. Final scores available."
  5. Archived OKR is moved to the "Previous Quarters" tab; read-only.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (RTE wants to extend quarter): Admin can override quarter end date in ART settings; archive deferred.

##### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-01:** Given a user with RTE role, when they submit a new OKR with valid objective, at least 1 key result with target and unit, and a valid quarter/year, then the OKR is persisted and appears in the ART OKR list within 2 seconds.
- **AC-02:** Given an OKR with 3 key results, when a user edits the target of key result 2 after snapshots exist, then a "Target revised mid-quarter" badge appears on key result 2 and the audit log records the old and new target values.
- **AC-03:** Given the first day of a new quarter, when the cron job runs, then all active OKRs for the previous quarter are archived, a final snapshot is recorded for every key result, and no active OKR data is deleted.
- **AC-04:** Given an OKR with no strategic theme linked, when it is saved, then it appears in the Alignment Gap Report with the `UNLINKED` tag.
- **AC-05:** Given a user with PO role (not RTE), when they attempt to create an ART-level OKR, then the system returns a permission error and does not persist the record.

##### Business Rules

- BR-01: Maximum 10 active OKRs per ART per quarter.
- BR-02: Maximum 5 key results per OKR.
- BR-03: Key result `current` value cannot exceed `target * 1.5` (input validation; override available for stretch achievements with explicit RTE confirmation).
- BR-04: OKR `artId` and `teamId` are mutually exclusive at the scope level: an OKR is either ART-scoped (teamId null) or team-scoped (artId null referencing ART via team's artId).
- BR-05: Quarter/year combination is immutable after first snapshot is recorded.
- BR-06: Archived OKRs are retained indefinitely; not eligible for hard delete via UI (only via data export + admin purge).
- BR-07: OKR objective text must be unique within the same ART/team and quarter (case-insensitive deduplification warning, not hard block).

##### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** Enterprise teams (200–2000 devs) use OKRs in Notion, Lattice, or Google Sheets disconnected from their Jira/Rally delivery boards. RTEs report spending 4–8 hours per PI manually reconciling OKR health against delivery status. This is the "strategy tax" — overhead that reduces strategic responsiveness.

**Target segment:** RTEs and Portfolio Managers at Series B+ SaaS companies and mid-market enterprises running 3+ ARTs.

**Key interview question:** "When a key result falls below target mid-quarter, how long does it take you to identify which epics or features are contributing to the shortfall, and what tool do you use today?"

---

#### 16.1.2 Key Result Progress Tracking and Snapshots

##### Description

Enables POs, PMs, and the Copilot AI to update key result `current` values and persist timestamped snapshots. Snapshots feed trend charts (sparklines on cards, full charts on detail view) and drive the confidence score. The system supports both manual updates (PO entering a number) and automated updates via integration hooks (e.g., a Jira ticket count, a GitHub merge count, or a custom metric pushed via webhook).

##### Use Cases

**UC-04: Manual Key Result Update**

- **Trigger:** PO opens a team OKR, clicks a key result value to edit inline.
- **Pre-condition:** OKR is active. User has `PO` or `RTE` role on the team's ART.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. User clicks the current value field on the key result card.
  2. Inline number input appears pre-filled with current value.
  3. User enters new value and submits.
  4. System validates value is ≥ 0 and ≤ target * 1.5 (soft cap; confirmation dialog for override).
  5. System creates a `KeyResultSnapshot { id, keyResultId, value, recordedAt, recordedBy, source: MANUAL }`.
  6. Progress bar and percentage recalculate in real-time (optimistic UI update).
  7. If new value crosses a 25%/50%/75%/100% threshold, system fires a notification to the RTE and Business Owner.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (value lower than previous snapshot): System persists the lower value and adds a "Regression" badge to the snapshot in the history timeline; does not block save.

**UC-05: Automated Key Result Update via Integration**

- **Trigger:** A GitHub webhook event or Linear webhook event fires and matches a configured metric rule.
- **Pre-condition:** Admin has configured a metric rule mapping a webhook event to a key result ID and aggregation function (count, sum, last-value).
- **Main Flow:**
  1. Webhook fires `POST /api/webhooks/github` or `POST /api/webhooks/linear`.
  2. Handler checks for metric rules matching the event type and repo/project scope.
  3. Handler computes new aggregated value per rule's aggregation function.
  4. Handler calls internal `updateKeyResult(keyResultId, computedValue, source: AUTOMATED)`.
  5. Snapshot is created with `source = AUTOMATED`; displayed in timeline with a webhook icon.
  6. Threshold notifications fire identically to UC-04.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (webhook signature verification fails): Event is rejected; incident logged; no snapshot created.
  - A2 (no matching metric rule): Event is processed for other purposes (e.g., GitHub PR linking) but no KR update occurs.

**UC-06: View Key Result History and Trend**

- **Trigger:** User clicks on a key result card to open the detail drawer.
- **Pre-condition:** At least 2 snapshots exist for the key result.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. Detail drawer opens showing: objective context, KR description, target/current/unit, progress bar.
  2. Line chart renders all snapshots in chronological order with value on Y-axis and date on X-axis.
  3. A projected trend line (linear regression over last 4 snapshots) extends to quarter end date.
  4. If projected trend line will not reach target by quarter end, system displays a "At Risk" badge in amber.
  5. Snapshot log below the chart shows each entry: value, date, actor (or AUTOMATED), source icon.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (fewer than 2 snapshots): Chart replaced with "Not enough data yet. Update this key result to see trends."

##### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-06:** Given a key result with `target = 100` and `current = 60`, when a user updates the value to 80 and saves, then a new snapshot is created with `value = 80, source = MANUAL`, the progress bar updates to 80%, and no threshold notification fires (thresholds: 25/50/75/100).
- **AC-07:** Given a key result at 74%, when a user updates it to 76%, then a threshold notification is dispatched to RTE and Business Owner within 5 seconds.
- **AC-08:** Given 5 snapshots on a key result, when a user opens the detail drawer, then a line chart renders all 5 data points and a projected trend line is visible extending to the quarter end date.
- **AC-09:** Given a projected trend that will not reach the target by quarter end, when the user views the key result card, then an "At Risk" badge is displayed in amber.
- **AC-10:** Given a GitHub webhook event with a matching metric rule, when the handler processes it, then a snapshot is created with `source = AUTOMATED` and the key result current value updates without manual intervention.

##### Business Rules

- BR-08: A maximum of 1 manual snapshot per key result per calendar day per user (deduplication; second update within same day overwrites previous value for that day).
- BR-09: Automated snapshots are not subject to the daily deduplication limit.
- BR-10: Snapshots from a closed quarter are immutable.
- BR-11: Projected trend uses linear regression over the most recent 4 snapshots minimum; if fewer than 4 snapshots exist, trend line is not rendered.
- BR-12: Confidence score displayed on OKR card = weighted average of per-KR progress percentages, where each KR has equal weight unless a custom weight is assigned by the RTE.

##### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** Key result updates are a high-friction manual ritual. Teams either skip updates (resulting in stale OKRs) or use dedicated OKR tools (Gtmhub, Perdoo) that lack any delivery context. The automation hook differentiates Cosmos by turning delivery events into OKR signals automatically.

**Target segment:** Engineering-led orgs where the RTE also owns engineering metrics (deploy frequency, PR throughput) and wants those signals to flow into OKR dashboards without manual data entry.

**Key interview question:** "Do you trust the OKR values your teams report today, or do you cross-check them against delivery data? How long does that cross-check take?"

---

### 16.2 Strategic Themes

#### Description

Strategic themes are the top-level organizational intent anchors in Cosmos. Each theme (`StrategicTheme { id, orgId, title, description, color, horizon, arts[] }`) represents a multi-quarter strategic bet owned at the portfolio level. Themes are linked to ARTs, which cascade them to epics and OKRs. The `horizon` field supports a three-horizon model (H1: Optimize/Grow, H2: Emerging, H3: Seed/Transform), enabling portfolio balance analysis. Color coding provides visual differentiation across all surfaces (portfolio kanban, program board, roadmap).

The strategic themes capability is the connective tissue that transforms Cosmos from an execution tool into a strategy-execution platform — the central claim of the portfolio wedge.

#### Actors / Personas

- **Portfolio Manager / VP Strategy:** Creates and owns themes; adjusts horizon assignments.
- **Business Owner:** Reviews theme health and approves theme-to-ART linkage.
- **RTE:** Assigns ARTs to themes; maps epics and OKRs to themes for their ART.
- **SAFe Copilot (AI actor):** Suggests theme assignments for unlinked epics; flags epics consuming budget without theme alignment.

---

#### 16.2.1 Create and Manage Strategic Themes

##### Description

Provides a dedicated theme management surface where Portfolio Managers create, edit, and retire strategic themes, assign horizon classifications, color-code them, and link them to one or more ARTs. Changes propagate immediately to all linked surfaces (portfolio kanban, roadmap, epic cards, OKR cards).

##### Use Cases

**UC-07: Create Strategic Theme**

- **Trigger:** Portfolio Manager clicks "New Theme" on the Strategic Themes settings page.
- **Pre-condition:** User has `PORTFOLIO_MANAGER` or `ADMIN` role on the org.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. User enters title (max 80 chars), description (max 500 chars).
  2. User selects horizon: H1, H2, or H3 from a radio group with tooltip explanations.
  3. User picks a color from a predefined palette of 12 colors (or enters a hex code).
  4. User selects one or more ARTs to link from a multi-select list of the org's ARTs.
  5. User saves. System persists the theme and propagates `theme.created` event.
  6. Theme appears in the theme list and is immediately available in all epic/OKR/roadmap dropdowns.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (duplicate title in same org): Warning shown; user may proceed (themes are differentiated by ID).
  - A2 (no ART linked): Theme is created as "Portfolio-only"; can be linked to ARTs later.

**UC-08: Edit Strategic Theme**

- **Trigger:** Portfolio Manager clicks Edit on an existing theme.
- **Pre-condition:** Theme is not archived.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. Edit drawer opens pre-filled with current values.
  2. User modifies any field. Color changes propagate to all epics, OKRs, and roadmap items linked to this theme immediately.
  3. User saves. Audit log records the change.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (horizon change from H1 to H3): System shows "Changing horizon will affect portfolio balance charts. Confirm?" dialog.

**UC-09: Archive Strategic Theme**

- **Trigger:** Portfolio Manager selects "Archive" from theme context menu.
- **Pre-condition:** Theme has no active (non-completed) epics referencing it, OR user confirms forced archive.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System checks for active epics with `strategicThemeId = this.id`.
  2. If none: theme status set to `ARCHIVED`; removed from all active dropdowns but retained in historical data.
  3. If active epics exist: system shows "X epics are still linked to this theme. Archiving will mark them as UNLINKED. Continue?" Confirmation required.
  4. On confirm: all linked active epics receive `strategicThemeId = null` and an audit entry noting the forced unlink.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (user cancels): No changes made.

**UC-10: Link Theme to ART**

- **Trigger:** RTE opens ART settings and adds a theme from the theme multi-select.
- **Pre-condition:** Theme exists and is active. User has `RTE` role on the ART.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. RTE selects themes from the multi-select on the ART settings page.
  2. System updates `StrategicTheme.arts[]` to include the ART.
  3. Theme is now available in the ART's epic, OKR, and roadmap item dropdowns.
  4. Existing ART epics without a theme are surfaced in the "Unlinked Epics" alert banner.

##### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-11:** Given a Portfolio Manager with the correct role, when they create a theme with title, horizon H2, a valid color, and at least one ART linked, then the theme is persisted and immediately appears in the epic creation dropdown for that ART.
- **AC-12:** Given a theme with color #3B82F6 linked to 4 epics, when the Portfolio Manager changes the color to #EF4444, then all 4 epic cards and roadmap items update to the new color within 3 seconds without page reload.
- **AC-13:** Given a theme linked to 2 active epics, when a Portfolio Manager attempts to archive it without confirmation, then the system displays a warning listing the 2 epics and requires explicit confirmation before proceeding.
- **AC-14:** Given an archived theme, when a user opens the epic creation form, then the archived theme does not appear in the strategic theme dropdown.

##### Business Rules

- BR-13: Maximum 20 active strategic themes per org.
- BR-14: Color must be unique within the org's active themes (prevents ambiguity on visual surfaces).
- BR-15: Horizon values are restricted to H1, H2, H3; no custom horizons.
- BR-16: A strategic theme must belong to an org (orgId is required and immutable after creation).
- BR-17: Archived themes cannot be directly reactivated; they must be recreated (preserving archival intent). Audit trail from the archived theme is retained.

##### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** Portfolio Managers at SAFe organizations lack a single place to define strategic themes and see how those themes translate into funded work. Themes live in PowerPoint; epics live in Jira. The linkage between them is manual and breaks down within one PI.

**Target segment:** Portfolio Managers and Chief Product Officers at enterprises with 5+ ARTs running SAFe 5.0 or 6.0.

**Key interview question:** "If I showed you a dashboard that told you exactly what percentage of your current PI capacity is aligned to each strategic theme, would you trust the data enough to use it in a board presentation?"

---

#### 16.2.2 Theme-to-ART Alignment View

##### Description

Provides a visual heat-map or bar chart showing, for each strategic theme, the distribution of epic WSJF scores, budget allocation, and feature count across linked ARTs. Enables Portfolio Managers to detect imbalance: themes with no ART capacity committed, ARTs spending capacity on unlinked epics, or over-concentration of H1 work crowding out H2/H3 investment.

##### Use Cases

**UC-11: View Theme Alignment Heat Map**

- **Trigger:** Portfolio Manager opens the "Theme Alignment" tab in the Strategic Themes module.
- **Pre-condition:** At least 2 strategic themes and 2 ARTs exist with linked epics.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System queries all active epics grouped by `strategicThemeId` and `artId`.
  2. Heat map renders: rows = themes, columns = ARTs; cell value = count of IMPLEMENTING epics + total WSJF score.
  3. Color intensity encodes WSJF concentration (higher score = darker cell).
  4. Cells for theme/ART combinations with zero epics render in gray with "No investment" tooltip.
  5. User can click any cell to drill into the filtered epic list.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (epics exist with no theme): A pseudo-row "Unaligned" is added to the heat map, surfacing unlinked investment.

**UC-12: View Horizon Balance Donut**

- **Trigger:** Portfolio Manager opens the "Portfolio Balance" sub-panel.
- **Pre-condition:** At least 1 epic linked to a theme with a horizon assignment exists.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System aggregates total WSJF score (or story point estimate) by horizon across all active themes.
  2. Donut chart renders with three segments: H1 (blue), H2 (amber), H3 (green).
  3. Percentage labels on each segment. Target bands (configurable: default H1 70%, H2 20%, H3 10%) shown as arc markers.
  4. Out-of-band segments are highlighted with a warning icon.
  5. User can hover a segment for breakdown by ART.

##### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-15:** Given 3 themes linked to 2 ARTs with epics, when the Portfolio Manager opens the Theme Alignment tab, then the heat map renders with 3 rows, 2 columns, and correct WSJF aggregations per cell.
- **AC-16:** Given unlinked epics (no strategicThemeId), when the heat map renders, then an "Unaligned" pseudo-row appears showing the aggregate WSJF of all unlinked epics.
- **AC-17:** Given configured target bands of H1: 70%, H2: 20%, H3: 10%, when the current portfolio is H1: 85%, H2: 12%, H3: 3%, then all three segments are flagged as out-of-band with warning icons.

##### Business Rules

- BR-18: WSJF aggregation for the heat map uses `Epic.wsjfScore`; if `wsjfScore = null`, the epic is counted in feature count but excluded from WSJF sum with a footnote.
- BR-19: Target horizon bands are configurable per org by an Admin; defaults are H1: 70%, H2: 20%, H3: 10%.
- BR-20: The heat map only includes epics with `status NOT IN (DONE, REJECTED)`.

##### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** Portfolio review meetings spend 30–45 minutes manually calculating horizon balance from spreadsheets. Automated balance visualization with drill-through to epics would reclaim this time and enable real-time portfolio rebalancing decisions.

**Target segment:** CPOs and Portfolio Managers running SAFe at scale (>3 ARTs), preparing for quarterly portfolio reviews and board updates.

**Key interview question:** "How do you currently assess whether your portfolio investment is balanced across strategic horizons, and how confident are you in that assessment on any given Tuesday morning?"

---

### 16.3 Strategy Map

#### Description

The strategy map is a visual canvas that renders the causal flow from strategic themes through OKRs, epics, and features down to team-level delivery. It is inspired by the Balanced Scorecard strategy map concept but adapted for SAFe: each column represents a level of the SAFe hierarchy (Portfolio → ART → Team → Sprint), and each row traces a theme's hypothesized cause-and-effect path through the delivery stack. The `strategy-map` server action drives the data layer; the frontend renders a directed graph using a DAG layout engine.

This capability directly addresses the investor due-diligence angle: it produces a single visual artifact that answers "show me how your strategy connects to what your engineers are building this sprint" — the question no incumbent tool answers in one screen.

#### Actors / Personas

- **Business Owner:** Views the map during PI Planning to validate strategy-execution alignment.
- **Portfolio Manager:** Uses the map for board and investor reporting.
- **RTE:** Uses the map to identify disconnected epics (epics that exist without a theme path reaching them).
- **SAFe Copilot (AI actor):** Generates natural-language summaries of the strategy map for export.

---

#### 16.3.1 Strategy Map Canvas

##### Use Cases

**UC-13: Render Strategy Map for an ART**

- **Trigger:** RTE navigates to the Strategy Map module for their ART.
- **Pre-condition:** ART has at least 1 strategic theme, 1 OKR, and 1 epic linked to a theme.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System fetches: strategic themes linked to ART, OKRs for ART and its teams, epics with `strategicThemeId` set, features per epic, sprint stories (count only).
  2. DAG layout engine places nodes: Theme nodes (top) → OKR nodes → Epic nodes → Feature nodes (bottom).
  3. Edges drawn: Theme → OKR (theme linkage on OKR), OKR → Epic (same theme or explicit linkage), Epic → Feature.
  4. Node color inherits from theme color. Node size encodes WSJF score (epics) or confidence % (OKRs).
  5. User can zoom, pan, and click any node to open its detail drawer without leaving the canvas.
  6. Orphan nodes (epics with no theme, OKRs with no linked epic) render in gray at the edge of the canvas with a "Disconnected" label.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (too many nodes to render clearly): System auto-collapses feature nodes into "N features" aggregate nodes; user can expand per epic.

**UC-14: Export Strategy Map**

- **Trigger:** User clicks "Export" and selects PNG, SVG, or PDF.
- **Pre-condition:** Map has rendered at least once.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System renders the canvas off-screen at 2x resolution.
  2. For PDF: system also calls `safe-copilot` action to generate a 3-sentence AI summary of the map's key themes and gaps.
  3. File is prepared and downloaded to the user's browser.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (Copilot summary generation fails): Export proceeds without the summary; a note "AI summary unavailable" is appended to the PDF.

**UC-15: Filter Strategy Map by Theme or Horizon**

- **Trigger:** User uses the filter panel on the left side of the map canvas.
- **Pre-condition:** Strategy map is rendered.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. User selects one or more themes from the filter checkboxes, or selects a horizon (H1/H2/H3).
  2. Map re-renders showing only nodes connected to the selected themes/horizons.
  3. Non-matching nodes fade to 20% opacity rather than disappearing (preserving spatial context).
  4. Filter state is persisted in URL query params for shareability.

##### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-18:** Given an ART with 2 strategic themes, 3 OKRs, 6 epics, and 14 features, when the strategy map is opened, then a DAG renders with theme nodes at the top, OKR nodes in the second level, epic nodes in the third level, and feature aggregate nodes at the bottom, all within 4 seconds.
- **AC-19:** Given 2 epics with no strategicThemeId, when the map renders, then those 2 epics appear as gray "Disconnected" nodes at the edge of the canvas.
- **AC-20:** Given a user filtering by H2 themes only, when the filter is applied, then only nodes connected to H2 themes are fully visible; all other nodes are at 20% opacity.
- **AC-21:** Given a successful map render, when the user exports to PDF, then the exported file contains the map image and a 3-sentence AI summary of key themes and gaps.

##### Business Rules

- BR-21: Strategy map is read-only — editing of nodes must be done in their respective modules (OKR, Epic, Theme). The map is a visualization surface only.
- BR-22: Maximum 200 nodes rendered simultaneously; above this limit, feature nodes are auto-collapsed.
- BR-23: Edge connections are computed at render time from existing data relationships; no manual edge drawing is supported.
- BR-24: Filter state in URL params must be shareable without authentication leakage (params are filtered before URL is copied; org ID is not included in sharable URL fragment).
- BR-25: Strategy map data is refreshed every 60 seconds in background; a "Last updated X seconds ago" indicator is shown. Manual refresh button available.

##### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** The most frequently cited pain point by VP Strategy and CTO buyers in SAFe tooling evaluations is the inability to answer the question "what is our strategy actually producing?" in a single view. Strategy maps exist in Miro and Figma but are static, disconnected from live data, and require manual maintenance.

**Target segment:** CTOs and VP Engineering at Series C+ SaaS companies and large enterprises preparing for annual planning, board meetings, or investor due diligence.

**Key interview question:** "If you had a live strategy map that showed which epics your team is building this quarter and which strategic themes they're connected to, would you use it in your next board presentation? What would need to be true for you to trust the data?"

---

### 16.4 Roadmap Items

#### Description

Roadmap items (`RoadmapItem { id, artId, epicId, quarter, year, confidence, notes }`) place epics on a delivery timeline by quarter and year, assign a confidence percentage (0–100) to signal commitment level, and support scenario planning by allowing multiple roadmap configurations. The roadmap view aggregates across ARTs for a portfolio-level view, or scopes to a single ART for team-facing planning. Confidence levels drive visual encoding (solid bar = high confidence, hatched = medium, outline = low) consistent with SAFe PI objectives' committed/uncommitted convention.

Roadmap items link directly to epics, inheriting theme color and WSJF score for visual prioritization. An epic without a roadmap item is surfaced in the "Unscheduled Epics" backlog rail.

#### Actors / Personas

- **Portfolio Manager:** Manages the portfolio-level roadmap; assigns epics to quarters; sets confidence.
- **RTE:** Manages the ART-level roadmap; reviews portfolio assignments and adjusts team capacity.
- **Business Owner:** Views the roadmap for stakeholder communication; exports for board decks.
- **PM:** Reviews roadmap to validate epic sequencing aligns with feature dependencies.
- **SAFe Copilot (AI actor):** Warns when roadmap density exceeds ART capacity; suggests resequencing based on WSJF and dependency graph.

---

#### 16.4.1 Create and Manage Roadmap Items

##### Use Cases

**UC-16: Add Epic to Roadmap**

- **Trigger:** Portfolio Manager or RTE drags an epic from the "Unscheduled Epics" rail onto a quarter column in the roadmap.
- **Pre-condition:** Epic exists with `status NOT IN (DONE, REJECTED)`. User has `RTE` or `PORTFOLIO_MANAGER` role.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. On drop, system creates a `RoadmapItem` with `epicId`, `artId`, `quarter`, `year`, `confidence = 50` (default), `notes = ""`.
  2. Epic card appears in the quarter column with theme color fill and WSJF score badge.
  3. System checks capacity: if total story point estimate of all roadmap items in that quarter exceeds ART average quarterly velocity by more than 20%, an amber capacity warning banner appears.
  4. System also checks for unresolved dependency links: if any `DependencyLink` from this epic's features references a feature scheduled for a later quarter, a dependency conflict alert fires.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (epic already on roadmap in a different quarter): System shows "This epic is already scheduled for Q{n} {year}. Move it here?" confirmation. On confirm, old roadmap item is deleted and new one created.

**UC-17: Adjust Roadmap Item Confidence**

- **Trigger:** User clicks the confidence badge on a roadmap item card and drags the slider or enters a value.
- **Pre-condition:** Roadmap item exists.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. Confidence slider (0–100) appears inline.
  2. User sets value. Card visual encoding updates in real-time: 0–33% = outline only, 34–66% = hatched fill, 67–100% = solid fill.
  3. User clicks away or presses Enter. Value is persisted.
  4. If confidence drops below 34%, an in-app notification is sent to the Business Owner linked to the epic's theme.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (user sets confidence to 0): System asks "Mark as dropped from roadmap?" If confirmed, roadmap item is soft-deleted and epic moves back to Unscheduled rail.

**UC-18: View Portfolio Roadmap (Multi-ART)**

- **Trigger:** Portfolio Manager navigates to the Portfolio Roadmap page.
- **Pre-condition:** At least 2 ARTs have roadmap items.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System fetches all roadmap items across all ARTs in the org for the selected year range (default: current year + next year).
  2. Roadmap renders as a horizontal timeline: rows = ARTs, columns = quarters.
  3. Each cell contains epic cards for that ART/quarter combination, color-coded by strategic theme.
  4. A legend at the top maps theme colors to theme names.
  5. Clicking an epic card opens the epic detail drawer without navigating away.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (more than 8 ARTs): System collapses ARTs into groups and provides an expand control.

**UC-19: Scenario Planning — Duplicate Roadmap**

- **Trigger:** Portfolio Manager clicks "New Scenario" from the roadmap toolbar.
- **Pre-condition:** A base roadmap exists with at least 5 roadmap items.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System creates a deep copy of all current roadmap items, tagged with `scenarioName` (user-provided, max 50 chars).
  2. The scenario is visible in a scenario switcher dropdown in the roadmap toolbar.
  3. User can move, remove, and re-assign roadmap items within the scenario without affecting the "Base" roadmap.
  4. User can click "Compare Scenarios" to see a side-by-side diff (Base vs. selected scenario): items added, removed, moved between quarters, confidence changes.
  5. User can "Promote to Base" which overwrites the base roadmap with the scenario (confirmation required; base roadmap is archived before overwrite).
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (user promotes without archiving acknowledgment): System forces a confirmation dialog listing what will change in the base roadmap.

**UC-20: Export Roadmap for Stakeholder Presentation**

- **Trigger:** User clicks "Export" and selects format (PNG, PDF, CSV).
- **Pre-condition:** Roadmap has at least 1 roadmap item.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. For PNG/PDF: system renders the roadmap canvas at print resolution; includes legend, confidence encoding key, and export timestamp.
  2. For CSV: system generates a flat table with columns: epic title, ART, quarter, year, confidence, theme, WSJF score, notes.
  3. File is downloaded to the user's browser.

##### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-22:** Given an unscheduled epic, when a Portfolio Manager drags it to Q3 2027 on the roadmap, then a RoadmapItem is created with quarter=3, year=2027, confidence=50, and the epic card appears in the Q3 2027 column within 1 second.
- **AC-23:** Given a roadmap item with confidence=80, when the user changes confidence to 30, then the card visual updates to outline-only encoding and a notification is dispatched to the Business Owner within 5 seconds.
- **AC-24:** Given a portfolio roadmap with 3 ARTs, when the Portfolio Manager views it, then all ARTs render as separate rows with their respective roadmap items grouped by quarter, and theme colors are consistent with the theme legend.
- **AC-25:** Given a base roadmap with 8 items, when the Portfolio Manager creates a scenario, removes 2 items, and opens Compare Scenarios, then the diff view shows exactly 2 items marked as "Removed in scenario".
- **AC-26:** Given roadmap items that aggregate to 150% of ART quarterly velocity for Q2, when the Portfolio Manager views the Q2 column, then an amber capacity warning banner is displayed on that column.
- **AC-27:** Given a CSV export request, when the download completes, then the CSV contains one row per roadmap item with all required columns (epic title, ART, quarter, year, confidence, theme, WSJF score, notes).

##### Business Rules

- BR-26: Maximum 25 roadmap items per ART per quarter.
- BR-27: An epic can appear on the roadmap at most once per scenario (same epic cannot be scheduled in two quarters within the same scenario).
- BR-28: Confidence value must be an integer between 0 and 100 inclusive.
- BR-29: Maximum 5 saved scenarios per ART per year; oldest scenario is archived automatically when the limit is exceeded, with a warning notification to the Portfolio Manager.
- BR-30: Scenario promotion is irreversible via the UI; the archived base is retained for 90 days in the audit trail and can be restored by an Admin.
- BR-31: Roadmap items for epics in `DONE` or `REJECTED` status are automatically moved to a "Completed/Removed" archive rail; they remain visible in historical views but do not appear in the active roadmap.
- BR-32: Capacity warning threshold (default 120% of average quarterly velocity) is configurable per ART by the RTE.
- BR-33: Year range for portfolio roadmap view is configurable between 1 and 5 years from the current year.

##### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** Product roadmaps exist in ProductBoard, Aha!, or Google Slides with no connection to team velocity, WSJF scores, or dependency graphs. Roadmap commitment levels are communicated verbally ("we think we can do this next year") rather than through a confidence metric visible to all stakeholders. Scenario planning for annual planning cycles is done in spreadsheets with no rollback.

**Target segment:** Portfolio Managers, CPOs, and Business Owners at mid-market and enterprise organizations (500–5000 employees) preparing annual and quarterly planning cycles.

**Key interview question:** "How long does it take you to produce a roadmap update for a board presentation, and how much of that time is spent manually pulling data from Jira, spreadsheets, and presentation tools? What would a 10-minute roadmap update capability be worth to you?"

---

### 16.5 Cross-Capability: Strategy-to-Execution Traceability

#### Description

The strategy-to-execution traceability capability is the integrated view that ties together all four capabilities in this section: it allows any user to start from an OKR key result that is at risk, trace it to the strategic theme driving it, see which epics are expected to contribute, navigate to the features in flight, and drill down to the sprint stories being worked on this week — all without leaving Cosmos. This full-stack traceability is what separates Cosmos from point solutions and constitutes the primary value proposition for the portfolio wedge.

The traceability chain is: `StrategicTheme → OKR → Epic → Feature → Story → Sprint`.

#### Actors / Personas

- **CTO / VP Engineering:** Navigates the traceability chain to understand delivery risk against strategic commitments.
- **RTE:** Uses traceability to prepare PI System Demo narratives.
- **Business Owner:** Uses traceability during Inspect & Adapt to diagnose why a KR missed its target.
- **SAFe Copilot:** Generates traceability reports on demand, summarizing the chain in natural language.

---

#### 16.5.1 Traceability Breadcrumb Navigation

##### Use Cases

**UC-21: Navigate Traceability Chain Top-Down**

- **Trigger:** User opens any OKR card and clicks "Trace to Delivery".
- **Pre-condition:** OKR is linked to at least one epic via strategic theme.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System opens a traceability panel: left column = OKR + key results, center column = linked epics (filtered by same theme), right column = features in those epics that are in `IN_PROGRESS` or `COMMITTED` status.
  2. User can expand any feature row to see its current sprint stories and their status (DONE/IN_PROGRESS/TODO).
  3. A progress summary at the top shows: "X of Y features on track, Z features at risk based on sprint burndown."
  4. Links on each node navigate to the full detail page for that entity.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (OKR linked to theme with no implementing epics): Center column shows "No implementing epics found for this theme. Consider creating an epic aligned to this objective."

**UC-22: Navigate Traceability Chain Bottom-Up**

- **Trigger:** Developer opens a story and clicks "Why does this matter?".
- **Pre-condition:** Story has a featureId, feature has an epicId, epic has a strategicThemeId.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System opens a read-only traceability breadcrumb: Story → Feature → Epic → Theme → OKR.
  2. Each level shows title, status, and a "Open" link.
  3. If any link in the chain is broken (e.g., epic has no theme), the breadcrumb shows a broken-link icon at that level with "Alignment gap: this epic is not linked to a strategic theme."
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (story has no feature): Breadcrumb starts at team level with "This story is not linked to a feature. Consider linking it to improve traceability."

**UC-23: Generate Traceability Report via Copilot**

- **Trigger:** RTE opens the Copilot sidebar and types "Generate a traceability report for Q3 OKRs".
- **Pre-condition:** OKRs exist for the specified quarter. Copilot has access to `okrs`, `strategic-themes`, `epics`, `features`, and `sprints` data.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. Copilot calls the `okrs`, `epics`, and `features` server actions to retrieve the relevant data.
  2. Copilot generates a markdown report: for each OKR, lists linked theme, status, and contributing epics with their current delivery status.
  3. Report is displayed in the chat thread with a "Download as PDF" button.
  4. Report is also saved to the ART's Knowledge Base (copilot upload) for future RAG queries.

##### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-28:** Given an OKR linked to a theme with 3 implementing epics and 8 features, when the user clicks "Trace to Delivery", then the traceability panel renders all 3 epics and 8 features, with story counts and status indicators, within 3 seconds.
- **AC-29:** Given a story linked to a feature, feature linked to an epic, epic linked to a theme, and theme linked to an OKR, when the developer clicks "Why does this matter?", then the traceability breadcrumb shows all 5 levels with correct titles and statuses.
- **AC-30:** Given an epic with no strategicThemeId, when the bottom-up breadcrumb reaches the epic level, then a broken-link icon and "Alignment gap" message are displayed at the epic level.
- **AC-31:** Given a Copilot request to generate a traceability report for Q3, when the report is generated, then it contains one section per OKR listing linked theme, current key result progress, and at least the title and status of each contributing epic.

##### Business Rules

- BR-34: Traceability panel is read-only; no entity edits are made from this view.
- BR-35: If an epic is linked to multiple themes, the traceability chain shows all themes it is linked to, with the primary theme (first assigned) highlighted.
- BR-36: Traceability breadcrumb is only shown on story detail pages when the story has a `featureId` set; stories not linked to features show a simplified breadcrumb from Story → Team.
- BR-37: Copilot-generated traceability reports are stored in the knowledge base with a TTL of 90 days; after 90 days they are purged from the vector store but the PDF download remains accessible if the user saved it.
- BR-38: Traceability data (the chain computation) is computed on-demand; no pre-materialized traceability graph is stored, ensuring data freshness at the cost of query time (target: < 3 seconds for chains up to depth 5).

##### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** The single most-cited differentiator in win/loss analyses against Jira Advanced Roadmaps, Rally, and VersionOne is the inability to answer "why is my team doing this work, and is it actually moving a strategic needle?" in real time without a data analyst. Traceability that requires BI queries or manual spreadsheet joins has a time-to-insight measured in days, not seconds.

**Target segment:** CTOs, VP Engineering, and Business Owners at organizations with 3–15 ARTs where alignment between strategy and delivery is a quarterly source of executive anxiety.

**Key interview question:** "In your last quarterly business review, when a key result was behind target, how long did it take to determine which delivery items were contributing, and what was the primary obstacle to getting that answer faster?"

---

### 16.6 Alignment Gap Detection and Alerts

#### Description

Alignment gap detection is an automated background capability — driven by the `anomaly-scheduler` cron job and the `flow-intelligence` server action — that continuously scans for structural misalignments between strategy and delivery and surfaces them as prioritized alerts. Gaps include: epics consuming budget with no theme linkage, OKRs approaching quarter-end with key results below 50% and no implementing epics in flight, roadmap items with high confidence but blocked features, and strategic themes with no ART investment for two or more consecutive PIs.

#### Actors / Personas

- **RTE:** Primary recipient of ART-scoped alignment gap alerts.
- **Portfolio Manager:** Receives portfolio-scoped gap summaries (weekly digest or on-demand).
- **SAFe Copilot:** Triggered by gap detection to suggest remediation actions.

---

#### 16.6.1 Alignment Gap Detection Rules

##### Use Cases

**UC-24: Automated Alignment Gap Scan**

- **Trigger:** `anomaly-scheduler` cron fires (default: daily at 06:00 UTC). Or triggered manually by RTE via "Run Gap Scan" button.
- **Pre-condition:** Org has at least 1 ART with active epics and OKRs.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System runs gap detection rules against current data state (see Business Rules BR-39 through BR-44).
  2. Each detected gap creates an alert record: `{ type, severity, artId, entityType, entityId, message, detectedAt, status: OPEN }`.
  3. Alerts are surfaced in the Notifications module, grouped by severity (CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW).
  4. In-app banners appear on the affected modules (OKR module shows banner for OKR-related gaps; Roadmap module shows banner for roadmap-related gaps).
  5. For CRITICAL gaps, RTEs receive an email notification in addition to in-app alerts.

**UC-25: Dismiss or Acknowledge Alert**

- **Trigger:** RTE clicks "Acknowledge" or "Dismiss" on an alert.
- **Pre-condition:** Alert status = OPEN.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. Acknowledge: alert moves to `ACKNOWLEDGED` status; remains visible in the alert list with a timestamp.
  2. Dismiss: alert moves to `DISMISSED` status; removed from active banner but visible in alert history. RTE must provide a dismissal reason (dropdown: "Accepted risk", "Will fix in next PI", "False positive", "Other").
  3. Both actions are logged in the audit trail.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A1 (gap is auto-resolved before user action): Alert automatically moves to `AUTO_RESOLVED` status when the underlying condition no longer applies (e.g., epic gets a theme assigned). Alert history shows resolution timestamp and trigger.

##### Acceptance Criteria

- **AC-32:** Given an epic with `status = IMPLEMENTING` and `strategicThemeId = null`, when the daily gap scan runs, then an alignment gap alert of type `UNLINKED_EPIC` with severity HIGH is created and an in-app banner appears on the Epic module.
- **AC-33:** Given an OKR with a key result at 30% progress with 20 days left in the quarter and no implementing epic in `IMPLEMENTING` status, when the gap scan runs, then an alert of type `OKR_AT_RISK` with severity CRITICAL is created and the RTE receives an email notification.
- **AC-34:** Given an alert in OPEN status, when the RTE dismisses it with reason "Accepted risk", then the alert moves to DISMISSED status, the in-app banner is removed, and the audit log records the actor, timestamp, and reason.
- **AC-35:** Given an alert in OPEN status for an unlinked epic, when the RTE assigns a strategic theme to that epic, then the alert automatically moves to AUTO_RESOLVED status within 60 seconds without manual action.

##### Business Rules

- BR-39 (Gap Rule 1 — Unlinked Epic): Epic with `status IN (PORTFOLIO_BACKLOG, IMPLEMENTING)` and `strategicThemeId = null` → severity HIGH.
- BR-40 (Gap Rule 2 — OKR at Risk): OKR key result with `(current/target) < 0.5` and fewer than 21 days to quarter end and no epic with `status = IMPLEMENTING` linked to the OKR's theme → severity CRITICAL.
- BR-41 (Gap Rule 3 — High-Confidence Roadmap Item Blocked): RoadmapItem with `confidence >= 67` and associated epic has ≥ 1 feature with all `DependencyLink.status = IDENTIFIED` (unresolved) → severity HIGH.
- BR-42 (Gap Rule 4 — Theme Starvation): StrategicTheme linked to an ART where zero epics have `status IN (ANALYZING, PORTFOLIO_BACKLOG, IMPLEMENTING)` for 2+ consecutive PI periods → severity MEDIUM.
- BR-43 (Gap Rule 5 — Budget Without Theme): Epic with `leanBudgetAllocation > 0` and `strategicThemeId = null` → severity HIGH.
- BR-44 (Gap Rule 6 — OKR Orphan): OKR exists for an ART/team but no key result has any snapshot after 30 days of creation → severity MEDIUM (stale/abandoned OKR).
- BR-45: Dismissed alerts are not re-raised for the same entity within the same quarter unless the underlying condition materially worsens (e.g., confidence drops further by >20 points).
- BR-46: Maximum 50 open alerts per ART at any time; oldest LOW-severity alerts are auto-archived when limit is exceeded.

##### Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem validated:** Alignment gaps are discovered reactively — at Inspect & Adapt, during a board meeting, or when a key result misses its target — rather than proactively in time to course-correct within the PI. Automated detection with push notifications transforms gap management from a retrospective activity to a real-time governance function.

**Target segment:** RTEs at organizations where PI Inspection & Adapt sessions consistently surface "we didn't know this was misaligned" findings — indicative of insufficient real-time visibility.

**Key interview question:** "In your last Inspect & Adapt, were there alignment gaps that surprised you? How many PIs in a row has that been true? What would you have needed to see those gaps three weeks earlier?"

---

## Large Solution: Solution Trains, Capabilities, LACE & Suppliers

### 17.1 Overview and Strategic Rationale

The Large Solution layer in SAFe 6.0 addresses the coordination challenge that emerges when a single Agile Release Train is insufficient to deliver a complex solution. Cosmos implements this layer as a first-class domain, enabling enterprises that operate multiple ARTs — whether building embedded systems, defense platforms, enterprise software suites, or regulated financial products — to manage cross-ART coordination, capability alignment, supplier relationships, and organizational transformation through a unified control plane.

From a market positioning standpoint, Large Solution support is the capability gate that separates Cosmos from mid-market Agile tools. Enterprises operating at this scale (typically 500–5000+ practitioners) represent the highest-value segment of the SAFe addressable market. These organizations currently rely on a fragmentation of Jira Advanced Roadmaps, custom SharePoint wikis, spreadsheet-based ROAM boards, and manual email coordination with suppliers. Cosmos unifies this into a coherent, event-driven, AI-augmented platform.

The domain models in this section — `SolutionTrain`, `Capability`, `SolutionEpic`, `LACE`, and `Supplier` — are persisted entities with full audit trails, RBAC enforcement, AI-assisted analysis, and real-time collaboration support via Liveblocks. Every entity in this section participates in the copilot RAG index and is exposed through the server action layer under `/actions/solution-trains`, `/actions/capabilities`, `/actions/solution-epics`, `/actions/lace`, and `/actions/suppliers`.

---

### 17.2 Solution Train Management

#### 17.2.1 Description

A Solution Train is the organizational construct that aligns multiple ARTs, suppliers, and other contributing entities around a shared solution. In Cosmos, a `SolutionTrain` is a top-level organizational entity scoped to an `orgId`. It aggregates ARTs, capabilities, solution epics, and a LACE. The Solution Train provides the coordination layer above individual ARTs while remaining below the Portfolio layer in the SAFe hierarchy.

Solution Train management allows Solution Train Engineers (STEs), Release Train Engineers (RTEs), and Enterprise Architects to create, configure, and govern the alignment of multiple ARTs toward a common product vision. This is the canonical entry point for large-scale SAFe adoption within an enterprise tenant.

#### 17.2.2 Actors and Personas

- **Solution Train Engineer (STE):** Primary owner of the solution train. Creates and configures trains, assigns ARTs, sets cadence parameters, and monitors cross-ART health.
- **Release Train Engineer (RTE):** Operates within one ART on the train. Views train-level artifacts that affect their ART.
- **Enterprise Architect (EA):** Defines capabilities and ensures technical coherence across ARTs.
- **Business Owner:** Monitors solution-level outcomes, reviews PI objectives, approves investment.
- **Solution Manager/PM:** Owns the solution vision, prioritizes the solution backlog, manages the capability roadmap.
- **Supplier Account Manager:** External or internal contact for supplier deliverables scoped to a solution train.

#### 17.2.3 Use Cases

**UC-17-01: Create Solution Train**

- **Trigger:** STE or admin navigates to `/solution-trains/new` and initiates solution train creation.
- **Pre-condition:** Org has at least two ARTs defined. User has `SOLUTION_TRAIN_ADMIN` permission.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. User opens the creation form.
  2. User enters `name` (required, 3–120 chars), `description` (optional, max 2000 chars).
  3. User selects one or more ARTs from the org's ART list to associate with the train.
  4. System validates that each selected ART is not already assigned to another active solution train.
  5. System creates the `SolutionTrain` record, associating the selected ARTs, initializing an empty `LACE`, empty `capabilities[]`, and empty `solutionEpics[]`.
  6. System publishes `solution_train.created` event to Inngest for downstream indexing and notifications.
  7. System redirects user to the new solution train's overview page.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A-1: If an ART is already assigned to another solution train, the system displays a conflict warning with the name of the conflicting train. User must deselect the ART or explicitly migrate it.
  - A-2: If the org is on a pricing tier below `ENTERPRISE`, the system displays an upgrade prompt instead of the creation form.
- **Exceptions:**
  - E-1: If name is a duplicate within the org, system returns a validation error with field-level feedback.

**UC-17-02: Assign or Remove ART from Solution Train**

- **Trigger:** STE navigates to the solution train's ART management panel and modifies the ART list.
- **Pre-condition:** Solution train exists. User has `SOLUTION_TRAIN_ADMIN` permission.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. STE opens the solution train settings page, navigates to "Assigned ARTs."
  2. STE selects an unassigned ART from the org to add, or selects a currently assigned ART to remove.
  3. For addition: system checks the ART is not assigned to another active solution train. If clear, association is created.
  4. For removal: system checks whether any in-progress capabilities or solution epics have features mapped to teams within the departing ART. If yes, system presents a dependency impact report.
  5. STE confirms the change (with or without acknowledging the impact report).
  6. System updates the `arts[]` array on `SolutionTrain`, emits `solution_train.art_assignment_changed` event.
  7. Affected capability and solution epic records are flagged for review.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A-1: If the ART being removed has unresolved cross-ART dependencies linked to the train, the system blocks removal until dependencies are resolved or explicitly overridden by a user with `FORCE_REMOVE` permission.
- **Exceptions:**
  - E-1: Network failure during update triggers optimistic rollback on the client with a retry option.

**UC-17-03: View Solution Train Health Dashboard**

- **Trigger:** STE, EA, or Business Owner navigates to `/solution-trains/[id]`.
- **Pre-condition:** Solution train exists with at least one ART assigned.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System renders the solution train overview page.
  2. Dashboard displays: number of assigned ARTs, total teams across all ARTs, active capabilities count, solution epics by status, cross-ART dependency health (ratio resolved/total), LACE meeting adherence score, and supplier SLA compliance summary.
  3. Each metric is a clickable drill-down to the corresponding sub-section.
  4. AI copilot panel surfaced inline with solution-train-scoped RAG context — pre-seeded with the last 3 PI cycles of data for this train.
  5. Real-time presence indicators show other active users viewing this train (Liveblocks).
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A-1: If no PIs have been executed yet, the health dashboard shows an onboarding checklist: "Add capabilities," "Define solution epics," "Configure LACE," "Add suppliers."
- **Exceptions:**
  - E-1: If underlying ART data is stale (>24h since last sync), a staleness banner is displayed with a manual refresh option.

#### 17.2.4 Acceptance Criteria

**AC-17-01-1:** Given a user with `SOLUTION_TRAIN_ADMIN` role, when they submit a valid solution train creation form with two or more ARTs, then a `SolutionTrain` record is persisted, the ARTs are associated, a LACE entity is auto-created, and the user is redirected to the train overview within 2 seconds.

**AC-17-01-2:** Given an ART already assigned to an active solution train, when a second solution train creation attempts to include that ART, then the system rejects the assignment with a descriptive conflict error identifying the owning train by name.

**AC-17-01-3:** Given an org on the `GROWTH` pricing tier (not `ENTERPRISE`), when a user navigates to the solution train creation page, then they see an upgrade prompt and cannot proceed with creation.

**AC-17-02-1:** Given a solution train with an assigned ART that has features mapped to active capabilities, when an STE initiates ART removal, then the system displays a dependency impact report listing all affected capabilities and features before allowing confirmation.

**AC-17-03-1:** Given a solution train with at least one completed PI cycle, when a Business Owner views the health dashboard, then all six health metrics (ART count, capability count, epic status, dependency health, LACE adherence, supplier SLA) are rendered with accurate real-time data.

**AC-17-03-2:** Given multiple users viewing the same solution train page simultaneously, when one user updates a capability status, then all other active users see the update reflected within 500ms via Liveblocks without a full page reload.

#### 17.2.5 Business Rules

- BR-17-01: A solution train requires a minimum of 2 ARTs. Single-ART configurations use the standard ART module, not the Large Solution layer.
- BR-17-02: An ART may belong to at most one active solution train at a time.
- BR-17-03: Solution trains are scoped to an `orgId`. Cross-org solution trains are not supported.
- BR-17-04: Deleting a solution train requires explicit confirmation and is a soft delete. All child entities (capabilities, solution epics, LACE records) are archived, not destroyed.
- BR-17-05: The Large Solution layer is gated behind the `ENTERPRISE` pricing tier feature flag. The feature flag key is `large-solution-enabled`.
- BR-17-06: Solution train names must be unique within an org (case-insensitive comparison).

#### 17.2.6 Market Research Hypothesis

**Problem Validated:** Enterprises running 3–10 ARTs have no tool that natively models the SAFe Large Solution layer. They synthesize it from Jira hierarchy plugins, Confluence pages, and PowerPoint program boards. The coordination overhead is 15–25% of an RTE's weekly time.

**Target Segment:** Organizations with 500–2000 practitioners, $50M–$500M software budgets, running SAFe at the Large Solution or Full configuration level. Dominant in aerospace, defense, automotive, financial services, and healthcare IT.

**Key Interview Questions:**
1. How do you currently coordinate work across multiple ARTs toward a shared solution? What tools are involved?
2. When a capability spans three ARTs, how do you track whether each ART's features are on track? How long does it take to get that view?
3. What is the biggest source of coordination waste between your ARTs today?

---

### 17.3 Capability Management

#### 17.3.1 Description

Capabilities are large solution-level behaviors or functions that span multiple ARTs. A capability is decomposed into features, each of which is owned by a single ART team. Cosmos models `Capability` as a first-class entity within a `SolutionTrain`, enabling solution-level backlog management, cross-ART feature decomposition, WSJF-driven prioritization at the capability level, and progress tracking rolled up from constituent features.

Capability management is the operational core of the Large Solution layer. Without it, enterprises cannot answer the fundamental question: "Is our solution on track?" Cosmos makes this question answerable in real time.

#### 17.3.2 Actors and Personas

- **Solution Manager / PM:** Owns the capability backlog. Creates, prioritizes, and governs capabilities.
- **Enterprise Architect (EA):** Validates that capabilities are architecturally coherent and enables cross-ART technical alignment.
- **Product Manager (PM per ART):** Decomposes capabilities into features for their ART's backlog.
- **STE:** Monitors capability progress across all ARTs. Escalates blockers.
- **RTE:** Tracks features within their ART that enable a given capability.
- **Business Owner:** Reviews capability business value and approves major prioritization changes.

#### 17.3.3 Use Cases

**UC-17-04: Create Capability**

- **Trigger:** Solution Manager navigates to `/solution-trains/[id]/capabilities/new`.
- **Pre-condition:** Solution train exists with at least one ART. User has `CAPABILITY_WRITE` permission.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. User opens the capability creation form.
  2. User enters `title` (required), `description`, and sets initial `status` (defaults to `FUNNEL`).
  3. User optionally links the capability to one or more `SolutionEpic` records within the same train.
  4. User optionally tags the capability with enabling ARTs (pre-populates `enabledBy[]`).
  5. System validates inputs. On success, persists the `Capability` record.
  6. System emits `capability.created` event. Copilot RAG index updated asynchronously.
  7. System redirects to the capability detail page.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A-1: User can create a capability directly from a solution epic's decomposition panel, pre-populating the `solutionEpicId` link.
  - A-2: User can import capabilities in bulk via CSV upload. System maps columns to capability fields with a preview/confirmation step.
- **Exceptions:**
  - E-1: If a capability title duplicates an existing capability on the same solution train, system warns but does not block (duplicates are allowed — user confirms intent).

**UC-17-05: Decompose Capability into Features**

- **Trigger:** Solution Manager or PM opens a capability and clicks "Add Feature."
- **Pre-condition:** Capability exists. At least one ART is assigned to the solution train.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. User opens the "Feature Decomposition" panel on the capability detail page.
  2. User clicks "Add Feature," selects the owning ART and team from dropdowns.
  3. User enters feature title, description, and optional WSJF sub-scores.
  4. System creates a `Feature` record with `capabilityId` linked, `epicId` null (solution-level feature).
  5. Feature appears in the owning ART's feature backlog with a `[CAPABILITY]` badge.
  6. System emits `capability.feature_added` event.
  7. Progress bar on the capability card updates to reflect 0% completion for the new feature.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A-1: User can link an existing feature from an ART's backlog to the capability rather than creating a new one. System updates the feature's `capabilityId`.
  - A-2: Copilot can suggest feature decompositions based on the capability description. User reviews and accepts/rejects each suggestion individually.
- **Exceptions:**
  - E-1: If the selected team belongs to an ART not assigned to the solution train, system rejects the assignment with an error.
  - E-2: If a feature is already linked to a different capability, system displays a warning and requires explicit confirmation to re-link.

**UC-17-06: Track Capability Progress**

- **Trigger:** STE or Business Owner views the capability detail page or the train-level capability board.
- **Pre-condition:** Capability has at least one linked feature with story-level decomposition.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. System aggregates progress data: for each linked feature, counts total stories, completed stories, story points planned vs. completed.
  2. System calculates capability-level percent complete = completed story points / total story points across all features.
  3. System renders a feature-by-ART grid showing each feature's status (color-coded), owning team, and point progress.
  4. System highlights features that are behind schedule (planned completion sprint has passed with incomplete stories).
  5. AI anomaly detection surfaces predictive risk: "Based on current team velocity, Feature X is at risk of missing PI boundary."
  6. STE can drill down from any feature cell to the owning team's sprint board.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A-1: If no stories exist under features, progress displays as "Not decomposed" with an action link to the feature backlog.
- **Exceptions:**
  - E-1: If underlying sprint data is stale, a staleness warning is displayed on the progress metrics.

**UC-17-07: WSJF Prioritization of Capability Backlog**

- **Trigger:** Solution Manager opens the capability backlog in prioritization mode.
- **Pre-condition:** Multiple capabilities exist on the solution train.
- **Main Flow:**
  1. User navigates to `/solution-trains/[id]/capabilities?view=wsjf`.
  2. System displays all capabilities in a WSJF scoring table with columns: User-Business Value, Time Criticality, Risk Reduction / Opportunity Enablement, Job Size, and computed WSJF score.
  3. User enters or adjusts WSJF sub-scores for each capability inline.
  4. System recalculates WSJF scores in real time and re-sorts the table.
  5. User can lock the sort order to produce a committed prioritization.
  6. System persists scores and emits `capability.wsjf_updated` event.
  7. Prioritized order is reflected on the capability roadmap.
- **Alternate Flows:**
  - A-1: Copilot can suggest WSJF scores based on capability description and linked strategic themes, presenting rationale for each score. User accepts or overrides.
- **Exceptions:**
  - E-1: If Job Size is zero, WSJF computation is blocked and field is highlighted in red.

#### 17.3.4 Acceptance Criteria

**AC-17-04-1:** Given a Solution Manager with `CAPABILITY_WRITE` permission, when they submit a valid capability creation form, then a `Capability` record is persisted with status `FUNNEL`, linked to the correct solution train, and appears in the capability backlog within 1 second.

**AC-17-04-2:** Given a CSV import of 50 capabilities, when the user completes the preview/confirmation step and confirms, then all 50 capabilities are imported within 10 seconds with accurate field mapping and a success summary report.

**AC-17-05-1:** Given a capability with two linked features across two different ARTs, when a story in Feature A is marked complete, then the capability's overall percent-complete metric updates within 2 seconds to reflect the new story point totals.

**AC-17-05-2:** Given a copilot-suggested feature decomposition, when the user accepts three of five suggested features, then exactly three `Feature` records are created; the rejected two produce no records and no side effects.

**AC-17-06-1:** Given a capability with features whose planned PI completion has passed and stories remain incomplete, when the STE views the capability detail, then the AI risk indicator is visible with a specific message identifying the at-risk feature by name and estimated delay in sprints.

**AC-17-07-1:** Given a capability with Job Size set to zero, when a user attempts to save WSJF scores, then the system blocks persistence, highlights the Job Size field in red, and displays an explanatory validation message.

**AC-17-07-2:** Given three capabilities with computed WSJF scores, when the Solution Manager locks the prioritization order, then the locked order persists across page refreshes and is reflected on the capability roadmap.

#### 17.3.5 Business Rules

- BR-17-07: A capability must belong to exactly one solution train. Cross-train capabilities are not permitted; use solution epics for cross-train alignment.
- BR-17-08: A capability's `status` follows the flow: `FUNNEL` → `ANALYZING` → `BACKLOG` → `IMPLEMENTING` → `DONE` or `REJECTED`. Backward transitions are allowed only by users with `CAPABILITY_ADMIN` permission.
